mechanism_narrative: The continued week-to-week recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT signals more daytime presence in Manhattan, which should raise RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as commuting-linked trips convert into shopping and dining visits.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT keep improving or remain elevated but RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to the last 4 weeks, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS jumps sharply, leisure demand shifts toward outdoor activity and away from indoor retail-recreation trips, so RETAIL_REC should fall within one to two weeks after a large PARKS increase.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If a PARKS increase of 10 points or more is followed by stable or higher RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both remain deeply depressed, the city is still operating under constrained commuting and office attendance, which suppresses retail-recreation demand and keeps RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both stay below -35 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain below -35 for two weeks but RETAIL_REC rises versus the prior 4-week mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in RESIDENTIAL indicates more time spent at home, which should mechanically reduce discretionary outings and push RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays elevated or rises further while RETAIL_REC is higher than in the prior 28 days, this mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in GROCERY_PHARM combined with a concurrent improvement in WORKPLACES implies more essential errand activity and daytime trips, which should spill over into higher RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises while WORKPLACES improves in the same week
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES both rise in a week but RETAIL_REC does not improve in the following week, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: A steep drop in TRANSIT below its recent range signals weaker access to commercial corridors, and retail-recreation mobility should decline over the next two weeks after that break in transit access.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -50 after being above -48 the prior week
failure_condition: If TRANSIT crosses below -50 after a prior week above -48 and RETAIL_REC does not weaken within 14 days, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES improve while TRANSIT remains deeply negative, office reopening is not being matched by broad commuting normalization, so retail-recreation demand should stay flat or fall over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises at least 3 points while TRANSIT stays below -45
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES rises by at least 3 points while TRANSIT stays below -45 and RETAIL_REC still rises over the next month, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-summer leisure regime, stronger PARKS mobility should crowd out indoor retail trips, so a continuing PARKS surge is expected to hold RETAIL_REC below its recent average over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from 17.3 to 42.6 across the four observed weeks
failure_condition: If PARKS remains elevated or rises further but RETAIL_REC increases above its last-4-week mean, the hypothesis is rejected.
